article: Boundary Contacts and Logarithmic Spectral Integrals
status_convention: New or completed means relative to the inspected repository sources and the explicitly identified target. No global priority, external peer review, arithmetic independence, interval certification, or proof-assistant formalization is asserted.

claims.domain: p,q are independent complex orders; Re(a)>0 and Re(b)>0; resonance p+q=-2m with integer m>=0; fixed or explicitly tracked cutoff coordinate.
claims.result: Finite ambient bivariate contact coefficients at every resonance, all mixed order derivatives, cutoff translations, sharp degree generators, and normally convergent ordinary subtractions.
inherited: First symmetric contact 1/2 at total order zero
limitations: Does not add an independent outer order weight
Does not classify higher cyclotomic colors or three independent tails
Ambient differentiation must precede restriction to a resonance
Alternating parity finite parts are kept distinct

claims.result: Explicit ordinary symmetric and alternating sums at p+q=-2, including two evaluations in pi, log 2, and rational numbers.
claims.domain: The general resonant formula has Re(a),Re(b)>0. The displayed evaluated example uses p=1,q=-3,a=1,b=2.

claims.result: Finite Stieltjes/Hurwitz-order-derivative dictionary for every contact jet; an explicit ordinary first-Stieltjes series; argument derivatives and integer/half-integer harmonic reductions.
claims.domain: The T formulas use Re(z)>0 and the V formulas Re(z)>1. Boundary series have Re(a),Re(b)>0 and their stated finite subtraction. Polygamma harmonic formulas with zeta(j+1) require j>=1.
inherited: Classical Hurwitz Laurent coefficients and argument-differentiation identities
Classical Gamma, polygamma, and generalized harmonic conversions

claims.result: Every scalar spectral derivative at zero for any finite number of positive quadratic masses is a massless Hurwitz derivative plus one ordinary absolutely convergent digamma integral.
claims.domain: a>0, integer N>=1, all mu_j>0, integer derivative order r>=1; principal logarithms with the branch conventions in the article.
limitations: An exact one-variable integral is not a claim of finite reduction to a smaller special-value alphabet

claims.result: Compact logarithmic cut densities for connected mass increments of every order, exact moment cancellation, coincident-mass limits, critical odd-weight ordinary sum, and fixed-regulator polynomial-weight transforms.
claims.domain: a>0, anchor beta>=0, integer r>=1, all nu_j>beta; the weighted finite parts use the explicitly fixed regulator.
inherited: Classical Cauchy jump representation and digamma resolvent
The local regularization hierarchy listed separately below
limitations: Replacing labeled masses at fixed N is distinct from deleting spectral factors

claims.result: Finite polynomial-logarithmic subtraction gives a finite Hurwitz-derivative baseline and one ordinary digamma integral for every even polynomial weight and every spectral derivative order.
claims.domain: Real polynomial P in (n+a)^2; a>0; N>=1 integer; all masses positive; r>=1 integer.
limitations: This full ordinary integral theorem concerns even polynomial weights. The odd-weight full scalar analogue remains a research question.

claims.result: Every derivative at every nonpositive integer spectral point follows by taking P(z)=product_j(z+mu_j)^m. The baseline is explicit and finite; the residual digamma integral is ordinary.
claims.domain: Integer m>=0 and r>=1; a>0 and all mu_j>0. The weight coefficients are held fixed under the spectral differentiation.
limitations: Does not supply a terminating Bessel-order recurrence or a finite reduction of every integral to a smaller special-value alphabet

claims.result: Beta/Gamma generating function, Stirling moments, generalized harmonic mass-collision coefficients, transform to height-one multiple polylogarithms with all fixed order derivatives, and half-lattice/bilateral kernels and anchored primitives.
claims.domain: Mellin formula Re(s)>0; polylogarithmic transform every complex s for |z|<1, with z=1 separately stated for integer s>=1; collisions in the stated strict polydisk; bilateral shifts in (0,1).
inherited: Euler beta integral and Gamma expansions
Height-one multiple-polylogarithm series and classical zeta(2,{1}^{r-1}) reduction
limitations: No priority claim for the classical inputs or the resulting familiar constants

claims.result: The local principal-part correction for polynomially weighted jets is restated with matching fixed-N normalization.
limitations: Not a new general regularized-trace or interaction-degree theorem

claims.result: Replace the final numerator term +24\zeta\alpha_5 by +24\zeta_5 in the fifth reciprocal-Gamma coefficient.
The diagonal continued alternating-square law at nonpositive orders, including every cutoff jet and translation, is inherited from Bilinear Tails and Determinants.
limitations: The new independent two-order theorem extends this result; it does not reattribute the diagonal result

claims.result: The all-index cubic Stieltjes finite-part germ and local counterterm admit the already-preserved finite Tornheim coefficient representation.
limitations: Further reduction to depth-one or another smaller arithmetic alphabet remains separate and open in this work

claims.result: The unrestricted unequal-even-order reconstruction problem and the whole gap-six family remain open.
limitations: This article proves no new determinant nonvanishing result and no arithmetic independence of evaluated zeta values

topics: Exact contact factorization and zero loci

evidence.analytic: Complete proofs in the article; independent internal mathematical review of sensitive derivations.
evidence.exact: 123 symbolic assertions in the two exact-result files.
evidence.decimal: 32 contact/Stieltjes diagnostics; independent density, scalar, polylogarithmic, and negative-point programs; all selected checks passed.
evidence.limits: Finite checks do not prove universal claims. Decimal diagnostics are not interval certificates.
